A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPOT-Trip and contain the complete corresponding main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, algorithms, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Foursquare and Yelp, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, data-sparsity experiments, and case studies in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Foursquare and Yelp experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including quantitative comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The knowledge-enhanced static preference module, ODE-based dynamic preference module, fusion mechanism, losses, and recommendation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Foursquare and Yelp data for out-of-town trip recommendation. The case studies also retain the same users and origin-only or destination-only query scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine baselines, including Base + KDDC, Base + CNN-ODE, and Base + PPROC. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the sparsity experiments, component replacements, and AR-Trip case studies.

E3.justification: The user-based 80/10/10 split, preprocessing, four evaluation metrics, training settings, and supplementary experiment protocols are unchanged. Removing a duplicated sentence about baseline hour-of-day inputs in Appendix C.4 does not change the documented setting.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same component-removal and replacement ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, data-sparsity tests, and case studies. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same statement about three repetitions and averaged results, together with Table 1's two-sided t-tests at p < 0.05. No seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains SPOT-Trip F1 scores of 0.0400 and 0.0399 and PairsF1 scores of 0.0109 and 0.0190 on Foursquare and Yelp, respectively.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–3, the model and loss equations, Appendix A's approximate-posterior formulation and ELBO derivation, and Appendix C.3's metric definitions remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task-novelty claim, dual-preference modeling contributions, and performance claims, including improvement of up to 17.01%.

C2.justification: The interpretations of semantic information, component contributions, sampling, and parameter sensitivity remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 retains the single-endpoint query limitation, and Appendix E retains the discussion of repeated recommendations and error propagation.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's page 1 footnote identifying the SPOT-Trip code repository, without supplying a replacement pointer elsewhere. Other implementation details and dataset/baseline-code access information remain unchanged. This establishes loss of access guidance, not that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and Appendix B discussion are retained, with unchanged positioning relative to out-of-town recommendation, trip recommendation, knowledge graphs, and neural ODE research.

P1.justification: v3 updates Hao Miao's affiliation and email and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 publication information. Appendix C.4 removes a duplicated sentence and makes small tense and capitalization edits; the overall narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All nine figures and four tables retain their content, captions, and structure. Layout changes are limited to the first-page footnote/footer area and slight text and table reflow around pages 17–18.

improvement.justification: Removing the only SPOT-Trip code-access pointer modestly weakens reproducibility guidance. The duplicated-sentence removal and small language corrections improve polish but do not offset that loss. The scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall decline is limited.
